subject: Cardinal AI — streaming sessions left open causing retry storms & 5xx spike
messages:
From: Rebecca Liu <rebecca@cardinal.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@cardinal.ai
Date: 2026-11-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observed spike: 5xx/stream timeouts this morning

Hi Sean,

We're seeing a sudden spike of 5xx (mostly 502/504) and client-side timeouts across our streaming chat product since 07:40 PT. A couple details:

- Errors surface as stalled streams on the client after ~30s; clients then aggressively retry with exponential backoff which appears to amplify the error rate.
- Our ops team captured a short span of traffic showing a large number of connections that remain open with no data ("zombie" sockets).
- We tried restarting local SDKs and it reduced symptom frequency for a short window.

We need immediate assistance — this is impacting live conversations for paying customers and triggering PagerDuty. Can you escalate?

I've attached a short CSV of request counts and a small PCAP. Happy to hop on a call.

Thanks,
Rebecca
VP, Product
Cardinal AI

Attachments: cardinal_prod_error_report.csv, pcapsocket_zombies_1103.zip

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rebecca Liu <rebecca@cardinal.ai>
Date: 2026-11-03T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observed spike: 5xx/stream timeouts this morning

Quick triage notes (first 30m):

- Observed pattern: high ratio of long-idle TLS connections from a subset of Cardinal host IPs. These sockets show 0 bytes for 20–120s then client resets; the runtime sees many partial KV cache entries held open.
- Resource pressure: ephemeral allocator bump on the serving hosts (NVIDIA GPU nodes) and connection-handler thread queues filling up -> requests get queued and hit our 30s request timeout -> 502/504 surface.
- Retry amplification: clients are configured with a short retry window + no jitter on some SDK versions (v1.2.0). That causes synchronized reconnect waves.

Immediate mitigations I recommend we enact now (low risk):
- On Cardinal side: set TCP keepalive to 45s and enable application-level pings every 20s.
- On Redwood side (temporary): enable a short-lived circuit breaker per-client-IP (drop after 5 consecutive 504s) and increase front-end request timeout to 45s to prevent premature 502s during transient spikes.
- Roll a temporary routing rule to route Cardinal traffic to a less-loaded pod pool for 2h to reduce queuing.

I'll push a config change to the staging cluster and test; we can promote if we see the expected drop in active queued requests. Uploading a small Kibana snippet in the ticket.

- Aditya
Lead, Serving Runtime

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Rebecca Liu <rebecca@cardinal.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-03T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observed spike: 5xx/stream timeouts this morning

Rebecca — thanks for the capture. Per Aditya's notes, please try the following immediate client-side workarounds while we push server-side guardrails:

1) Client keepalive: enable/force application-level pings every 20s and TCP keepalive interval = 45s.
2) Retry behavior: add randomized jitter to retries and use an exponential backoff starting at 200ms up to 8s (do not retry on 5xx more than 3 times).
3) SDK version: avoid v1.2.0 for now; upgrade to v1.2.3 which contains our backoff fixes.

I'll send a short runbook and can stay on the line while you apply the change. We're also enabling a temporary routing and circuit-breaker on our side now.

Attachments: cardinal_streaming_20261103_kibana_snippet.log

- Monica
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Rebecca Liu <rebecca@cardinal.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Observed spike: 5xx/stream timeouts this morning

Monica/Sean — applied the keepalive and jitter changes on edge; we're seeing immediate improvement in the error rate (5xx down ~60%). However customers are asking for an executive point of contact and potential credit for the interruption to service.

Can Redwood prepare an incident summary and attend a 4pm PT review with our CTO and Head of Ops? Also please confirm the expected remediation timeline for the permanent fix.

Thanks,
Rebecca

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-03T17:42:00-07:00
Subject: Cardial AI escalation — exec brief and next steps

Team — summary and actions for exec briefing (4pm PT):

- Impact: Cardinal AI experienced a 5xx spike between 07:40–10:30 PT caused by a combination of client-side idle sockets and synchronized retry waves. Short-term mitigations reduced visible 5xx by ~60%.
- Root cause (working hypothesis): client SDKs holding idle connections + no jitter on retries -> socket buildup -> request queueing -> timeouts at 30s -> 502/504.
- Immediate work we did: recommended client keepalive/jitter, enabled per-client IP circuit-breaker, bumped front-end timeout to 45s, and routed traffic away from overloaded pod pool.
- Next steps (owner / ETA):
  * Aditya: patch runtime to proactively evict idle sockets and add a lightweight keepalive probe (ETA 48h).
  * Monica: draft incident summary and credit proposal for Cardinal (ETA 2h).
  * Lauren: coordinate exec review deck and join 4pm PT call (ETA 1h).

I'll lead the exec call and include a short A/B comparison of before/after error rates + proposed SLA remediation offer. If we need finance approval for credits, loop in Lauren's stakeholders.

- Sean
Sr. Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
